findings.title: canManage() grants global group management for VIEW-only permission
findings.body: The no-arg `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so any admin with only the `view` scope on the all-groups resource passes. `requireManage()` is used to guard `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, and `canManage()` is also reached via `root.groups()`. A view-only admin can therefore create top-level groups. It should check only `MANAGE`. The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` repeats the error by saying VIEW or MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes the resource id, not the group id
findings.body: In the `findByType` callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. For V2 the resource name is the group id, and `getId()` returns the authz resource's own UUID. The lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. The result is evaluated against the wrong resource: specific group permissions are ignored, and groups can be granted or denied based on all-groups policies instead. `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` then returns resource UUIDs instead of group ids, so the `UserModel.GROUPS` filter used by user search and count does not match real group ids. The type query also returns the "Groups" type resource itself. Both uses should be `groupResource.getName()`, and the type resource should be skipped.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource is missing
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource` returns null when the schema is unsupported or the type resource is not found. The code then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which is likely to throw an NPE instead of denying. A null check before the call should return false.

findings.title: Javadoc inaccurate for canManage() and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()
findings.body: The `canManage()` javadoc says it also returns true for VIEW permission on groups. That is wrong for a manage check, and it documents the bug in `GroupPermissionsV2`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` javadoc says it returns a "Stream of IDs" but the method returns `Set<String>`.
